The expanded sanctions target Iran's digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping sectors.

title: Prince Harry quits board of wildlife charity after rangers’ human rights abuses
description: <p>Spokesperson for Duke of Sussex says he remains an ‘active and avid supporter’ of African Parks’ mission</p><p>The Duke of Sussex has stepped down from the board of a major African wildlife charity that had been at the centre of a human rights controversy.</p><p>Prince Harry’s spokesperson confirmed he was no longer a trustee of <a href="https://www.africanparks.org/">African Parks</a>, which <a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq54dgv2p29o">admitted last year </a>that human rights abuses were committed by its rangers in the Republic of the Congo.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/aug/24/prince-harry-quits-board-wildlife-charity-african-parks-human-rights-abuses">Continue reading...</a>

title: US strikes a vessel in the eastern Pacific, killing 2 people in first attack in months
description: <p>US Southern Command has struck another vessel in the eastern Pacific, killing two accused of trafficking drugs</p><p>After a pause of more than two months, the US military announced Monday that it once again carried out a strike on a vessel in the eastern Pacific Ocean, killing two people accused of trafficking drugs.</p><p>It brings the overall death toll to 223 people killed in 67 strikes during the nearly year-long US campaign of bombing alleged drug boats off Latin America’s Caribbean coast and in the eastern Pacific Ocean. US Southern Command says the campaign has resulted in the destruction of 64 speedboats, three “low-profile” ships and a semisubmersible craft.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/24/vessel-strike-eastern-pacific">Continue reading...</a>

title: Trump announces new 50% tariff on Canadian cars, trucks and steel
description: <p>Move is latest deterioration in trade relations between neighbors with historically strong economic ties</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump">Donald Trump</a> announced a new 50% <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/trump-tariffs">tariff</a> on automobiles and crucial raw materials from <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/canada">Canada</a>, the latest deterioration in trade relations between the two neighbors with historically strong economic ties.</p><p>The US president said that the increased tariffs would start on 1 January 2027 on all cars, trucks, automobile parts and steel. He also derided the nation’s tariffs on American farmers, writing on social media that Canada has been “ripping off” the US “for years”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/24/canada-tariff-increase-trump-auto">Continue reading...</a>

title: Mark Carney says Canada can’t accept US trade deal that would weaken French language
description: <p>Prime minister praised for rejecting US trade proposal as Trump shows little interest in retreating from dispute</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/24/are-you-a-canadian-boycotting-us-products-wed-like-to-hear-from-you"><strong>Are you a Canadian boycotting US products? We’d like to hear from you</strong></a></p></li></ul><p>Mark Carney said on Monday that while American negotiators saw the French language in Canada as an “irritant … in Quebec, these are rights,” days after receiving widespread praise from political leaders for rejecting a US trade proposal that many perceived as weakening the country’s Francophone culture.</p><p>The prime minister’s remarks came hours after the US president, Donald Trump, showed little interest in retreating from the spat, posting on social media that Canada had been “ripping off the United States of America for years” and threatening a swath of new, economically devastating tariffs on cars and trucks.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/24/canada-trade-deal-trump-mark-carney-french-language">Continue reading...</a>

title: Australia news live: Sydney trains plagued by morning cancellations due to ‘urgent’ repairs to overhead wires
description: <p>Commuters warned journey may take an extra 45 minutes as ‘limited’ buses replace north short trains. Follow today’s news live</p><ul><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">breaking news email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p>Transport for NSW has put on “limited” buses replacing trains for Sydney’s north shore this morning, with major cancellations and delays across multiple lines.</p><p>The problem, <a href="https://transportnsw.info/alerts/details/09d4014cdd5a41295ca505af6b5e9bea9c8e52fd">we’re told</a>, is “urgent overhead wiring repairs at Chatswood”.</p><p>Limited buses are replacing trains from Gordon, all stations to Chatswood only due to urgent overhead wiring repairs at Chatswood. An unscheduled rail shuttle service will run between Hornsby and Gordon in both directions.</p><p>Trains that normally terminate at North Sydney and Berowra continue as tabled while Train services that normally end/start from Lindfield and Gordan will now end/start from North Sydney. Please note that some services will be cancelled to reduce congestion and avoid longer delays.</p><p>Those travelling from the north, ie through Hornsby, options are to come by Strathfield as well and also connect with the Metro at Epping.</p><p>The north, as you know, for the T1 North Shore is also connected to the Western line, so we are going to be running a reduced frequency from the west as well, unfortunately, this morning.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/live/2026/aug/25/australia-news-live-sydney-trains-delays-cancellations-albanese-gst-wa-one-nation-coalition-secret-harbour-election-tax-reform-royal-commission-antisemitism-icac-victorian-rail-loop-alan-jones-trial-ntwnfb">Continue reading...</a>

title: Victorian premier Ben Carroll pushes ahead with rail loop plan after hinting at pause
description: <p>A day after suggesting other projects were more important to Victorians, Carroll says train line will go ahead but at a slightly reduced cost</p><ul><li><p><strong>Get our </strong><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl"><strong>breaking news email</strong></a><strong>, </strong><a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3"><strong>free app</strong></a><strong> or </strong><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl"><strong>daily news podcast</strong></a></p></li></ul><p>The Victorian premier, Ben Carroll, has made an about-face, committing to pushing ahead with the first stage of the Suburban Rail Loop while promising to reduce its total cost by about 6%.</p><p>Carroll will on Tuesday announce changes to the scope of the first stage of the project, known as SRL East – a 26km stretch of tunnels between Cheltenham and Box Hill – estimated to save $1bn.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/aug/24/victorian-premier-ben-carroll-pushes-ahead-with-srl-spend-despite-hinting-at-pause">Continue reading...</a>

title: Australia has just 12,000 sea lions left – and ‘carnage’ may await them as bird flu takes hold, scientists warn
description: <p>Virus has already caused catastrophic losses in pinnipeds in South America and sub-Antarctica, particularly among pups</p><ul><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">breaking news email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p>Scientists have warned deadly H5 bird flu could cause “carnage” for Australia’s seal and sea lion populations after detection of the virus in long-nosed fur seals in South Australia.</p><p>SA <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/23/fur-seal-death-first-australian-mainland-mammal-h5-bird-flu">confirmed Australia’s first case in a mammal </a>on Saturday after a dead long-nosed fur seal found at Beachport on the Limestone Coast tested positive for H5N1.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/25/australia-has-just-12000-sea-lions-left-and-carnage-may-await-them-as-bird-flu-takes-hold-scientists-warn">Continue reading...</a>

title: UK to use Ukraine battlefield data to train AI to protect sensitive sites
description: <p>London and Kyiv in deal to help stop protesters and hostile states targeting military bases and critical infrastructure</p><p>AI models trained on Ukrainian battlefield data will be used to stop protesters and foreign states targeting UK defence sites, railways and energy plants under a deal struck between London and Kyiv.</p><p>Private companies will also be given access to the vast trove of data from Ukraine’s Avengers AI lab to help build new systems, the first agreement of its kind in the UK.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/aug/24/uk-to-use-ukraine-battlefield-data-to-train-ai-to-protect-sensitive-sites">Continue reading...</a>

title: Vuelta a España: giant hail forces stage three abandonment in Pyrenees
description: <ul><li><p>Huge hailstones prompt organisers to act 15km from end</p></li><li><p>Riders seen heading into hotel on route to take cover</p></li></ul><p>A torrential hailstorm in the French Pyrenees forced the abandonment of the ⁠third stage of the Vuelta a España on Monday.</p><p>With 15 kilometres (9.32 miles) remaining of the 174km route ⁠from Gruissan to Font-Romeu, the ​skies darkened as the peloton neared the top of the Col de Mont-Louis and huge hailstones began ⁠bouncing off the tarmac and pelting the riders.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/aug/24/vuelta-a-espana-giant-hail-forces-stage-three-abandonment-in-pyrenees">Continue reading...</a>

title: ‘Fix that little spot’: Danish PM hits back at unsolicited beauty tip from cosmetic surgeon
description: <p>Mette Frederiksen, who received message on returning from Ukraine, advises  women to embrace self-acceptance</p><p>Sick of getting unsolicited beauty tips on social media, the Danish prime minister, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jun/01/denmarks-mette-frederiksen-agrees-centre-left-coalition-after-months-of-uncertainty">Mette Frederiksen</a>, rebuffed a male cosmetic surgeon’s offer to “fix” her and advised women in similar situations to embrace self-acceptance.</p><p>Frederiksen, a Social Democrat and Denmark’s second female prime minister, posted on Instagram that she had just returned from a trip to Ukraine, where she was subjected to air raid sirens, when she found a message proposing some help with her appearance.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/24/danish-pm-mette-frederiksen-beauty-tips-kyiv">Continue reading...</a>

title: US threatens severe sanctions against countries with economic ties to Iran
description: <p>Washington launches campaign to isolate Tehran but it is unclear whether it will apply measures to China</p><p>The US has threatened to impose severe sanctions against any country or entity maintaining economic ties with Iran, hoping to achieve with economic measures what military means have so far failed to do.</p><p>It is unclear, however, how far the Trump administration is prepared to go in confronting China, Iran’s biggest trading partner, which has signalled its resistance to US economic pressure to cut off links with an ally.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/24/us-severe-sanctions-economic-ties-iran">Continue reading...</a>

title: Man arrested on suspicion of arson after fire at car park used by Gatwick passengers
description: <p>Blaze near Crawley destroyed 140 vehicles, damaged nearby businesses and led to power cuts on Saturday night</p><p>A man has been arrested on suspicion of arson after a fire tore through a car park used by people flying from Gatwick airport, destroying about 140 vehicles.</p><p>The blaze erupted at Caldyne business park near Crawley, about eight miles from the airport just after 9pm on Saturday. Images showed vehicles on fire and enormous plumes of smoke rising close to overhead power lines.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/aug/24/man-arrested-on-suspicion-of-arson-after-fire-at-car-park-used-by-gatwick-passengers">Continue reading...</a>

title: Reform would evict social housing tenants over unkempt gardens
description: <p>Plan part of a wider policy to remove foreign nationals from social homes and prioritise young British-born couples</p><p>Social housing tenants will be evicted if they fail to keep their gardens well maintained under a Reform UK government, the party has announced.</p><p>Lee Anderson, the party’s chair, said that if Reform came to power it would insist that those in social rented homes would be required to keep their properties decorated and gardens looked after.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/aug/24/reform-evict-social-housing-tenants-poor-garden-maintenance">Continue reading...</a>

title: Problems brewing for the proper pint as Camra membership falls
description: <p>Cost of living has hit campaign group while multinationals are threatening to squeeze out independent  breweries</p><p>For centuries, the wooden real ale pump has been the hallmark of a good British boozer. But now problems are brewing for the proper pint, as the Campaign for Real Ale has seen its membership sink to an eight-year low and its accounts show it is firmly in the red, making an £800,000 loss last year.</p><p>Real ale is a traditional draught cask beer, a “living” product that is produced and stored in its cask. It differs from a cold, fizzy lager, in which the yeast is killed and carbon dioxide is added. Real ale contains live yeast so it continues fermenting until it is served.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2026/aug/24/camra-campaign-for-real-ale-beer-breweries-pubs">Continue reading...</a>

title: Rupert Lowe set to be paid as much for divisive posts on Elon Musk’s X as for being MP
description: <p>Restore Britain leader paid up to £1,476 an hour by platform, which critics say is financially incentivising inflammatory content</p><p>Rupert Lowe, the leader of Restore Britain, is on course to earn as much from the social media platform X as he does from his salary as an MP, after surging income from posts that include demands for mass deportations.</p><p>Lowe has earned £932 an hour for his posts on X, formerly Twitter, since the start of the year, according to his own declarations in the register of MPs’ financial interests, which detail how many hours he has spent on X for each payment he received from the platform.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/aug/24/rupert-lowe-restore-britain-earn-same-on-x-as-being-mp-elon-musk">Continue reading...</a>

title: Alfalfa sprouts linked to food-poisoning outbreak in 15 states, US officials say
description: <p>Everything Sprouts recalls products after CDC says agency is aware of dozens of food-poisoning cases nationally</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/healthcare">US healthcare</a> officials recently said a food-poisoning outbreak tied to alfalfa sprouts and involving multiple germs had sickened people in at least 15 states.</p><p>Officials announced the outbreak after documenting more than three dozen cases in Minnesota and Wisconsin. On Friday, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said the agency was aware of at least 55 cases nationally, including four people who had been hospitalized.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/24/food-poisoning-alfalfa-sprouts">Continue reading...</a>

title: French tourist dies in California’s Death Valley after being stranded in heat
description: <p>Man, 68, was left searching for help in 116F weather after his car became stuck in mud along remote park road</p><p>A French tourist recently died in <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2023/jul/22/death-valley-tourism-extreme-weather-california">Death Valley national park</a> after a car mishap left him stranded in 116F (47C) weather.</p><p>The visitor, identified as 68-year-old Pierre Michel Formosa, was traveling with another French man along the park’s remote West Side Road when their vehicle became stuck in mud near Queen of Sheba Mine Road.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/24/french-tourist-death-valley-park">Continue reading...</a>

title: US immigration officers reassigned to screen South African refugees and find ‘unlawful’ voters
description: <p>Exclusive: internal correspondence reveals USCIS anti-fraud officers shifted on to two ‘high-priority’ initiatives</p><p>All US immigration officers working for a key anti-fraud unit have been reassigned by Donald Trump’s administration to focus on screening South African refugees and alleged “unlawful” voters.</p><p>Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate (FDNS) immigration officers have been shifted full-time on to two “high-priority” initiatives, according to internal correspondence seen by the Guardian, leaving US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) unable to provide officers to train asylum officers in “the near future”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/24/uscis-immigration-officers-reassigned">Continue reading...</a>

title: NYPD to investigate another video of people emerging from manhole
description: <p>Video posted on social media shows three people climbing out of sewer system at 4am, months after similar reports</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/new-york">New York City</a>’s police department (<a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/nypd">NYPD</a>) says it is investigating a recent video of three people emerging from a manhole in the latest such episode to cause <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jun/07/new-york-manhole-mole-people">mystery</a>.</p><p>Posted to TikTok on Friday, the <a href="https://www.tiktok.com/@ricardyfabre/video/7676468411987168542">video</a> showed three people – one after the other – climbing out of a manhole at 4.19am on 18 August wearing headlamps and black overalls near Madison Square Garden.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/24/nypd-investigation-video-people-manhole">Continue reading...</a>

description: As governments and private investors worldwide pour billions into nuclear fusion, it’s worth remembering that Russia has been a pioneer in this field going back to the 1950s, and continues to act as a key tech incubator, AtomInfo Center head Alexander Uvarov told Sputnik.
